mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but SPX returns are negative over 60 days more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment above 6% signals economic weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE exceeds 6% but SPX returns are positive over 20 days more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High FEDFUNDS and CPI indicate tight monetary policy and inflation, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: Both proxies are high but SPX returns are positive over 20 days more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening cycle, higher FEDFUNDS predicts negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS rises in a tightening cycle but SPX returns are positive over 20 days more than 50%.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing PAYEMS indicates strong employment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: PAYEMS increases but SPX returns are negative over 5 days more than 40%.

mechanism_narrative: INDPRO below 95 indicates supply weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO below 95 but SPX returns positive over 60 days more than 50%.

mechanism_narrative: Slow GDP growth and high unemployment indicate recession, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: Both proxies indicate weakness but SPX returns are positive over 20 days more than 40%.

mechanism_narrative: In late expansion, increasing HOUST signals strength, leading to positive returns.
failure_condition: HOUST increases in late expansion but SPX returns are negative over 60 days more than 50%.
